title: Resource allocation after round 10: shift toward high-risk exploration and potentially new barriers
question: How should bounded agent capacity be allocated to maximize the chance of a genuine advance on HYP-2de84d42?
rationale: All investigated routes to sub-sqrt(p) universal ECDLP on the residual hard class are closed or negative at toy sizes; recent rounds spent much capacity reviewing/formalizing elementary, likely known results. Expected value is highest for (a) broad, cheap-test high-risk exploration (only channel for a breakthrough) and (b) open mathematical questions with a realistic chance of a genuinely new, publishable barrier.
claims: Target allocation per round: ~40% frontier exploration (2-3 frontier-explorer agents, cheapest decisive tests), ~30% strongest open mathematics (tightness N-c of interpolation bounds; lower bounds in richer algebraic models with division/rational functions/branching), ~15% formalization only for new or barrier-central statements, ~15% review (mandatory before integration/write-up, batched).
Concurrency: up to 6 parallel bounded agents observed stable in round 10; keep <= 6.
next_action: Apply from the next free capacity; revisit after each package.
notes: User reminder (2026-11-03) to optimize for the best possible result; PI decision.
